title: Multi-Step Forms
description: Learn how to build forms that span multiple steps or pages.

data.text: **Multi-step forms** break long forms into smaller, manageable sections. They reduce cognitive load, allow per-step validation, and improve completion rates by showing progress.
A multi-step form keeps all data in one state object and shows only one step at a time. The user advances by clicking Next or Back, and validation runs before moving forward.

data.text: Show users where they are in the form. A simple progress bar or step labels reduces abandonment.

data.title: Progress Bar

data.text: Validate the current step before allowing the user to advance. This gives immediate feedback and prevents frustration at the end of a long form.

items.question: Should I persist multi-step form data?
items.answer: Yes. Use localStorage or URL state so users do not lose data if they refresh or navigate away accidentally.

items.question: Can I use a library for wizards?
items.answer: Yes. Libraries like React Hook Form Wizard or Formik Multi-Step simplify state and validation.

items.question: How do I prevent users from skipping steps?
items.answer: Disable Next until the current step is valid. Avoid showing direct navigation links to later steps.

items.question: Should I save the form after each step?
items.answer: If the form is long, consider auto-saving to the server or localStorage after each step.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Multi-step forms reduce cognitive load by splitting tasks.
Track the current step with state and render conditionally.
Show a progress indicator so users know where they are.
Validate each step before allowing advancement.
data.takeaway: Wizards make long forms feel approachable. Next, you will learn how to handle file uploads, which require special care in React.
